A reviewer claims this correctness issue:
  title: Null/undefined dereference on coupon returned by findCoupon
  lines: 2-3 (new file)
  rationale: findCoupon(cart.code) will return null or undefined when no coupon matches (e.g., cart.code is missing, expired, or invalid). The very next line unconditionally accesses coupon.amount, which throws a TypeError at runtime whenever findCoupon returns a falsy value.
If the caller passes a cart object that has no code property, cart.code is undefined. Passing undefined to findCoupon likely causes it to return null/undefined or look up a literally-undefined key, compounding the null-dereference on the next line. There is no guard or early-return for a missing code.

The ONLY context you may use is this hunk:
File: checkout.ts
Hunk: @@ -1,1 +1,3 @@
Lines show NEW-file line numbers; + added, - removed, space unchanged.
   1   function priceWithCoupon(cart) {
   2 +   const coupon = findCoupon(cart.code);
   3 +   return cart.total - coupon.amount;

Is the finding real and supported by THIS hunk? Try to refute it before agreeing. Report your outcome (upheld/refuted), your confidence, and your reasoning.

response.raw: {"outcome":"upheld","confidence":0.92,"reasoning":"The hunk shows `const coupon = findCoupon(cart.code)` immediately followed by `return cart.total - coupon.amount` with no null/undefined guard between them. A function named findCoupon is conventionally expected to return null/undefined when no match is found, and the code unconditionally dereferences coupon.amount, which throws a TypeError if coupon is falsy. The hunk itself contains the entire risky pattern — no external context is needed to see the missing guard. The only uncertainty is findCoupon's actual contract (it could theoretically always return a coupon or throw itself), which is not visible here, but the lookup-by-code semantics make a missing-match return path the overwhelmingly likely behavior. The finding is supported by this hunk."}
